Brief 012 round 3 · Forma · 2026-10-15 · Option 1: the Tech redrawn in line · Option 2: four icons · cosplay sheets · silhouette test. Faces, bodies and hair come from the A white-on-charcoal set (Codex, A portrait + lineup as references). Qwen Turbo spend this round $0.057; ceiling total $1.809 of $3.00. 1. Tech in line (option 1)

Eight crafted outfits for the Tech in the others' white-on-charcoal language, bare arms and relaxed stance kept, visor dark and unlit (it lights only when he works). Each lineup redraws only the third figure; the Scout, Fixer and Enforcer are unchanged (compare with the baseline).

2. Four icons (option 2)

One team thread (white on charcoal, chrome, matte technical fabric, visitors from a nearby timeline). Each person pushed into a distinct style with one signature item that is theirs alone, a silhouette you could name from a shadow, a personal accent (checked below against the signals) and one detail. Five Codex takes per person plus one Qwen wildcard.

3. Cosplay sheets

Front and back turnaround with three numbered callouts per sheet (signature item, two key pieces). Would someone build this? The back views are invented by the model from the front: check them before anyone cuts cloth.

4. Silhouette test

Black fills of every lineup, plus the whole lineup at play scale: the tallest figure 56 px high after the 38 degree camera's foreshortening (height x cos 38 = 0.788), shown at native size (the real size) and at 5x. Two numbers per lineup: true-scale silhouette overlap (IoU after aligning feet and centre; lower = more distinct) and the distance between width profiles (width over height, row by row; higher = more distinct). The worst (closest) pair matters most. Figures: 0 Scout, 1 Fixer, 2 Tech, 3 Enforcer.

Reading: the eight Tech-in-line lineups are numerically and visually the baseline (a different Tech outfit moves the lineup's silhouettes very little). L1 has the best worst-case separation; L3 is the weakest because three of the four wear long coats. IoU rises for the icon lineups because wider coats fill shared space, so use the profile distance and the 50 px view together, not IoU alone.

All clear dE 20. Tightest: the Enforcer's ink blue against the rivals' violet (24 to 25 painted), the Fixer's sienna against cone red (27 to 32 painted). The accents cover 0.1 to 2 percent of each figure, so they are a third read at best; at 50 px silhouette and the bone-on-charcoal blocking do the work. If colour is to be an identity read it needs an area (a lining, a panel), and the Enforcer's blue should move away from violet.
